root_cause.text: The authencesn instance creation in `crypto_authenc_esn_create()` did not validate that the ahash digest size is either zero or at least 4, allowing an invalid default authentication tag size (1–3 bytes) to be set via `inst->alg.maxauthsize`, which the AEAD core uses as the default authsize; this leads to an out-of-bounds access during ESN tail handling when 4 bytes of high-order sequence number data are moved on a too-short tag.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "While crypto_authenc_esn_setauthsize() already rejects explicit non-zero authsizes in the range 1..3, crypto_authenc_esn_create() still copied auth->digestsize into inst->alg.maxauthsize without validating it." and "AF_ALG could then trigger the ESN tail handling with a too-short tag and hit an out-of-bounds access." The patch adds a check `if (auth->digestsize > 0 && auth->digestsize < 4)` to reject such instances.
